what: Judge ask (a): does C3-partition (and H7, v1) challenge a honest dividing team that forms AFTER the 7-day warm-up? Answers the thin-test critique of C3's per-tick keystone (the sim's honest dividers all formed in week 1, so the warm-up exempted them). Generator prototypes/honesttwin_gen3.py places the twin + controls at T0 = day 10. No model calls.
pre_registration: Generator + prediction committed before scoring (predictions.md 'Honest twin AFTER the warm-up'). The points below are labelled POST-REGISTRATION notes (5.5 review), not a re-registration.
KNOWN_ANSWER_caveat: G1 is BUILT to match the swarm's footprint (burst co-registration, disjoint division, P ~ 1), so 'C3 challenges G1' is close to true BY CONSTRUCTION. What this test actually isolates is the WARM-UP's role -- whether a divider with the swarm's footprint, moved past day 7, is challenged (yes) -- not how often honest dividers occur.
NO_BASE_RATE_caveat: C3's honest false-challenge RATE equals how often honest teams divide a gated dataset undeclared on a real hub. This synthetic world cannot supply that base rate; the report says so in those terms.
synthetic_caveat: n = 1 per cell, rng seed 42, in a MINIMAL world: G1 (10 accounts), G2 (6), G3 (8) + 25 background accounts. It is NOT an injection into a full honest world.
no_dilution_caveat: G1 divides a repository of its OWN (teamdiv/corpus-v1), so no other first-puller lands in its 3600-s window. On a popular repo in a full world, concurrent honest first-pullers could raise its P (the dilution that protected honest cohorts in the full runs -- e.g. 161's swarm window held 1 honest account). So 'C3 challenges an honest divider' holds WITHOUT dilution; the real false-challenge rate needs both a base rate and realistic concurrent traffic.
first_score_disclosure: A FIRST score showed the approved_lab control (G2) CHALLENGED, because its declaration (request_access only) never reached orgs.jsonl and carried no repo-scoped access path, so c3_score_v3 never saw it as declared. The fixture was fixed in f75315b (real admin create_org + member-add orgs.jsonl rows + a repo-scoped access path) and re-scored; G2 is then exempt. (This is the F33/F34 'declaration stays untested until real orgs.jsonl rows exist' artefact.)
groups: G1 team_divider (fresh, undeclared, dividing, p_same = fraction pulling the same low shards); G2 approved_lab (aged, DECLARED via real orgs.jsonl + admin access-200, dividing) [control: must clear]; G3 cohort7 (fresh, undeclared, OVERLAP) [control]. Conditions: burst (<=9 min) | spread (0.2-1.8 h).

C3_partition_result.offline_and_pertick: CHALLENGES the G1 team_divider at low p_same, BOTH burst and spread: burst 0.0 (P 1.0), burst 0.2 (P 1.11), spread 0.0 (P 1.0), spread 0.2 (P 1.17). CLEARS at high p_same 0.5/0.8 (overlap -> distinct<4 or P>=1.6). G2 approved_lab EXEMPT (after the f75315b fix) in all cells; G3 cohort7 (overlap) cleared.
C3_partition_result.challenge_tick_vs_formation: the team first signs up at ~day 10.00 (T0); C3-partition challenges at ~day 10.01 (burst) / 10.03 (spread) -- within 1-3 ticks (~300-900 s) of formation. Per-tick honest accounts stepped up: 7 (burst), 5 (spread).

H7_result: Pages the G1 BURST divider at low p_same (burst 0.0, 0.2 = 1 false page each); clears burst 0.5/0.8 and ALL spread (sign-ups > 600 s -> no co-registration cohort). So H7 needs the tight sign-up burst; C3 (3600 s first-pull window) catches the spread divider too.
v1_result_MEASURED: v1 was RUN on all 8 gen3 cells (monitor.run, TimesFM off, built-in limits): 0 alerts and 0 pages on every cell. A within-quota divider (each account pulls 2 shards of a quota-2 repo) emits no impact-class item, consistent with results/v1_honest_zero.json / F04.

G4_just_minted_declared_lab.fixture: a FRESH (co-registering, created after day 7) + DECLARED (real orgs.jsonl admin create_org + member adds + repo-scoped admin access-200) + in-envelope dividing lab (8 accounts, 16 distinct shards of evalhold <= seats*quota = 20). Pre-registered before scoring (f-commit of honesttwin_gen3.py).
G4_just_minted_declared_lab.result: CONFIRMED. C3-partition EXEMPTS G4 in all cells (declared in-envelope, whatever its age -- only G1/teamdiv is challenged). H7 PAGES G4 in BURST (cohort 8, P=1.00, co-registration -- ignores declaration; still pages at p_same 0.8 since G4 is a fixed disjoint divider) and clears it in SPREAD (> 600 s, no co-registration). v1 was RE-RUN on the regenerated G4-included cells (monitor.run, TimesFM off) = 0 pages on all 8 (measured, not carried over from the pre-G4 run).
G4_just_minted_declared_lab.sham_org_hole: G4 makes the sham-org hole concrete with an HONEST fixture: a just-minted declared group with the swarm's footprint PASSES C3 (exempt), so a sham org that simply declares enough seats would pass too. Meanwhile H7 (which ignores declaration) false-pages this new honest lab (the F34 result). So neither detector cleanly handles the just-minted declared lab: C3's exemption is gameable by declaration, and H7 over-pages new honest labs -- which is exactly why the real fix is provenance (declared AND standing), not declaration alone.

prediction_outcomes: 1 CONFIRMED (by construction -- see KNOWN_ANSWER_caveat); 2 CONFIRMED (high p_same not challenged); 3 CONFIRMED (spread: H7 clears, C3 still challenges); 4 CONFIRMED (approved_lab exempt after fix, cohort7 cleared); 5 CONFIRMED by MEASUREMENT (v1 0 pages, run not inferred).
takeaway: C3's keystone 'challenges the swarm but no honest group' does NOT hold for honest teams that divide a dataset after the warm-up with the swarm's footprint -- those are challenged (burst and spread, low p_same). But this is a known-answer test (G1 is built to match the swarm), so it shows the WARM-UP's role, not a honest-divider frequency; C3's real honest false-challenge rate equals how often honest teams divide a gated dataset undeclared, which this synthetic world cannot supply. The per-tick '0 honest' on the fresh seeds reflects the sim placing every honest divider in week 1. This REINFORCES the thesis: C3 cannot tell the twin from the swarm, so it moves cost and does not separate.
spend: $0 (synthetic generation + CPU scoring + monitor with TimesFM off; no model calls).
